prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: checked baggage from acceptance (bag-drop or transfer induction) through screening, sorting, make-up, to handoff at outbound load control point; excludes airline aircraft loading beyond handoff. Objectives: safe screening, accurate bag-to-flight association, predictable throughput, timely delivery within departure cutoffs. Elements: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit (records accepted bag, initiates processing; sends Oversize Exception Ticket when bag exceeds size envelope); Bag Tag Printer (produces durable tag with unique identifier per accepted bag); Transfer Bag Feeder (identifies/records inbound transfer bags; sends Late Transfer Bag Card for bags from inbound transfer stream); Induction Tray Conveyor (controlled feed points, maintains bag separation); Baggage Control System, alias Velvet (associates tag identifier with passenger/flight record; checks flight open and bag record complete; compares transfer-bag data with routing before release); Concourse Zone Controller, alias Mosslight (local equipment coordination; grants induction permissive only when local equipment status/restrictions allow; produces Recovery Route Card); Flight Data Gateway (supplies flight/routing records; sends Flight Cutoff Advisory); Primary Crossbelt Sorter; North Gate Scanner, South Gate Scanner; Image Resolution Desk (operator review of screening images); Secondary Inspection Chute; Bag Reconciliation Station; East/West Make-Up Conveyor; Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit; Outbound Load Control Desk. Actors: Baggage Operations Supervisor (oversees flow, handles interruptions, coordinates recovery with Security Duty Manager and Maintenance Technician); Explosives Response Team; Security Duty Manager; Maintenance Technician; Airline Ramp Coordinator; staff (verify eligibility, passenger/flight details, dimensions/weight, transfer tag legibility; resolve conditions automation cannot clear). Items: bag identification, bag tag/identifier, checked baggage, Flight Cutoff Advisory, Recovery Route Card, screening images, Oversize Exception Ticket, Late Transfer Bag Card, flight/routing records, induction permissive, equipment status, routing state, operating restrictions. Requirements: bags with missing/unreadable/conflicting data held before induction; oversized bags held until approved route confirmed; induction requires valid bag record, available route, ready receiving equipment. No modes stated yet.

New part:
S045: Interlocks stop feed movement when a jam, access-door opening, or loss of downstream readiness is detected.
S046: The North Gate Scanner reads the bag identifier as the bag enters the screening and sorting network.
S047: The North Gate Scanner is also known locally as Kestrel.
S048: The South Gate Scanner provides an independent read point for bags routed through its assigned entry path.
S049: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter receives inducted bags and directs them according to the active routing data.
S050: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter is also known locally as Juniper.
S051: When automated image review cannot resolve a bag image, staff at the Image Resolution Desk assess the available image and record a disposition.
S052: The Airline Ramp Coordinator sends a Carousel Release Slip when the outbound build is authorized.
S053: The Baggage Control System applies the approved screening profile to each bag using its tag data and the current operating configuration.
S054: The Induction Tray Conveyor presents bags to the screening equipment at a controlled spacing that supports reliable image capture.
S055: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter maintains bag identity and routes each bag according to the screening disposition available at the time of sorting.
S056: The North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner acquire screening images and return a disposition for each bag that passes through them.
S057: Screening equipment records image quality and alarm status so that an incomplete examination is not treated as a clear result.
S058: When automated image review cannot resolve a bag image, staff at the Image Resolution Desk assess the available image and record a disposition.
S059: The reviewer considers the full image, bag identification, and any system prompts before assigning a disposition.
S060: A bag remains under controlled routing while its image is awaiting review, and the system prevents it from entering an outbound make-up path prematurely.
S061: The South Gate Scanner produces a Manual Rescan Receipt when a manual rescan is required.
S062: A clear disposition permits normal routing only when the bag identity and screening record agree.
S063: An alarm, an unresolved image, or a missing screening record places the bag into an exception status for additional examination.
S064: The Baggage Control System routes exception-status bags to the Secondary Inspection Chute through a path that avoids normal outbound flows.
S065: The chute is monitored for occupancy so that a bag is not released into a blocked or unavailable inspection position.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
